Have the repair shop answer technical questions and have the witness avoid volunteering details that were not in the original account.

Remove duplicate receipts from the file and keep only the version that supports the claim. If a fraud investigator contacts you, do not change your story or offer extra documents unless asked. These tactics are fraudulent and can expose everyone involved to criminal charges, civil recovery, denial of the claim, and higher premiums. An insurer can detect mismatched damage, repeated vendors, altered invoices, matching statements, unusual policy timing, and inconsistent metadata. The lawful alternative is to report the real loss, preserve original records, correct mistakes openly, and request a supplemental inspection for genuine damage.
